title: Recyclable and Low Fat Products
solution:
-- 1757. Recyclable and Low Fat Products
SELECT product_id
FROM Products
WHERE low_fats = 'Y' AND recyclable = 'Y';
notes: Simple WHERE clause filter with logical AND.

title: Find Customer Referee
notes: Trap: SQL three-valued logic. 'referee_id != 2' eliminates NULL values. Must check IS NULL or IFNULL.

title: Big Countries
solution:
-- 595. Big Countries
SELECT name, population, area
FROM World
WHERE area >= 3000000 OR population >= 25000000;
notes: Straightforward OR condition.

title: Article Views I
solution:
-- 1148. Article Views I
SELECT DISTINCT author_id AS id
FROM Views
WHERE author_id = viewer_id
ORDER BY id ASC;
notes: Use DISTINCT to remove duplicate views; sort ascending.

title: Invalid Tweets
solution:
-- 1683. Invalid Tweets
SELECT tweet_id
FROM Tweets
WHERE LENGTH(content) > 15;
notes: LENGTH() counts bytes; CHAR_LENGTH() counts characters.

title: Replace Employee ID With The Unique Identifier
solution:
-- 1378. Replace Employee ID With The Unique Identifier
SELECT eu.unique_id, e.name
FROM Employees e
LEFT JOIN EmployeeUNI eu ON e.id = eu.id;
notes: LEFT JOIN keeps all employees even if they don't have a unique identifier.

title: Product Sales Analysis I
solution:
-- 1068. Product Sales Analysis I
SELECT p.product_name, s.year, s.price
FROM Sales s
JOIN Product p ON s.product_id = p.product_id;
notes: Simple INNER JOIN on product_id.

title: Customer Who Visited but Did Not Make Any Transactions
solution:
-- 1581. Customer Who Visited but Did Not Make Any Transactions
SELECT v.customer_id, COUNT(v.visit_id) AS count_no_trans
FROM Visits v
LEFT JOIN Transactions t ON v.visit_id = t.visit_id
WHERE t.transaction_id IS NULL
GROUP BY v.customer_id;
notes: Classic Anti-Join: LEFT JOIN + WHERE right_table.key IS NULL.

title: Rising Temperature
solution:
-- 197. Rising Temperature
SELECT w1.id
FROM Weather w1
JOIN Weather w2 ON DATEDIFF(w1.recordDate, w2.recordDate) = 1
WHERE w1.temperature > w2.temperature;
notes: Do NOT use id = id - 1. Dates are not always strictly consecutive IDs; use DATEDIFF() = 1.

title: Average Time of Process per Machine
solution:
-- 1661. Average Time of Process per Machine
SELECT 
    a1.machine_id,
    ROUND(AVG(a2.timestamp - a1.timestamp), 3) AS processing_time
FROM Activity a1
JOIN Activity a2 
  ON a1.machine_id = a2.machine_id 
 AND a1.process_id = a2.process_id
 AND a1.activity_type = 'start' 
 AND a2.activity_type = 'end'
GROUP BY a1.machine_id;
notes: Self-join pairs start and end timestamps for the same machine and process.

title: Employee Bonus
solution:
-- 577. Employee Bonus
SELECT e.name, b.bonus
FROM Employee e
LEFT JOIN Bonus b ON e.empId = b.empId
WHERE b.bonus < 1000 OR b.bonus IS NULL;
notes: Remember 'OR b.bonus IS NULL' for employees with no bonus record.

title: Students and Examinations
solution:
-- 1280. Students and Examinations
SELECT 
    s.student_id, 
    s.student_name, 
    sub.subject_name,
    COUNT(e.subject_name) AS attended_exams
FROM Students s
CROSS JOIN Subjects sub
LEFT JOIN Examinations e 
  ON s.student_id = e.student_id 
 AND sub.subject_name = e.subject_name
GROUP BY s.student_id, s.student_name, sub.subject_name
ORDER BY s.student_id, sub.subject_name;
notes: CROSS JOIN generates all (student, subject) combinations so 0 attendance is preserved.

title: Managers with at Least 5 Direct Reports
solution:
-- 570. Managers with at Least 5 Direct Reports
SELECT m.name
FROM Employee e
JOIN Employee m ON e.managerId = m.id
GROUP BY m.id, m.name
HAVING COUNT(e.id) >= 5;
notes: Group by manager id and name to handle managers with identical names.

title: Confirmation Rate
solution:
-- 1934. Confirmation Rate
SELECT 
    s.user_id,
    ROUND(IFNULL(AVG(c.action = 'confirmed'), 0), 2) AS confirmation_rate
FROM Signups s
LEFT JOIN Confirmations c ON s.user_id = c.user_id
GROUP BY s.user_id;
notes: AVG(c.action = 'confirmed') calculates percentage directly in MySQL.

title: Not Boring Movies
solution:
-- 620. Not Boring Movies
SELECT id, movie, description, rating
FROM Cinema
WHERE id % 2 = 1 AND description != 'boring'
ORDER BY rating DESC;
notes: id % 2 = 1 checks for odd id; sort descending.

title: Average Selling Price
solution:
-- 1251. Average Selling Price
SELECT 
    p.product_id,
    IFNULL(ROUND(SUM(p.price * u.units) / SUM(u.units), 2), 0) AS average_price
FROM Prices p
LEFT JOIN UnitsSold u 
  ON p.product_id = u.product_id 
 AND u.purchase_date BETWEEN p.start_date AND p.end_date
GROUP BY p.product_id;
notes: Use IFNULL for products that have 0 units sold to avoid NULL/divide-by-zero.

title: Project Employees I
solution:
-- 1075. Project Employees I
SELECT 
    p.project_id,
    ROUND(AVG(e.experience_years), 2) AS average_years
FROM Project p
JOIN Employee e ON p.employee_id = e.employee_id
GROUP BY p.project_id;
notes: Standard AVG() and ROUND().

title: Percentage of Users Attended a Contest
solution:
-- 1633. Percentage of Users Attended a Contest
SELECT 
    contest_id,
    ROUND(COUNT(user_id) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Users), 2) AS percentage
FROM Register
GROUP BY contest_id
ORDER BY percentage DESC, contest_id ASC;
notes: Denominator is scalar subquery `(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Users)`.

title: Queries Quality and Percentage
solution:
-- 1211. Queries Quality and Percentage
SELECT 
    query_name,
    ROUND(AVG(rating / position), 2) AS quality,
    ROUND(AVG(rating < 3) * 100, 2) AS poor_query_percentage
FROM Queries
WHERE query_name IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY query_name;
notes: Filter out NULL query_names if any.

title: Monthly Transactions I
solution:
-- 1193. Monthly Transactions I
SELECT 
    DATE_FORMAT(trans_date, '%Y-%m') AS month,
    country,
    COUNT(id) AS trans_count,
    SUM(state = 'approved') AS approved_count,
    SUM(amount) AS trans_total_amount,
    SUM(IF(state = 'approved', amount, 0)) AS approved_total_amount
FROM Transactions
GROUP BY month, country;
notes: DATE_FORMAT(trans_date, '%Y-%m') groups by Year-Month.

title: Immediate Food Delivery II
solution:
-- 1174. Immediate Food Delivery II
SELECT 
    ROUND(AVG(order_date = customer_pref_delivery_date) * 100, 2) AS immediate_percentage
FROM Delivery
WHERE (customer_id, order_date) IN (
    SELECT customer_id, MIN(order_date)
    FROM Delivery
    GROUP BY customer_id
);
notes: Pick first orders per customer using tuple IN subquery.

title: Game Play Analysis IV
solution:
-- 550. Game Play Analysis IV
SELECT 
    ROUND(COUNT(a2.player_id) / COUNT(a1.player_id), 2) AS fraction
FROM (
    SELECT player_id, MIN(event_date) AS first_login
    FROM Activity
    GROUP BY player_id
) a1
LEFT JOIN Activity a2 
  ON a1.player_id = a2.player_id 
 AND a2.event_date = DATE_ADD(a1.first_login, INTERVAL 1 DAY);
notes: Self join to day after first login date.

title: Number of Unique Subjects Taught by Each Teacher
solution:
-- 2356. Number of Unique Subjects Taught by Each Teacher
SELECT teacher_id, COUNT(DISTINCT subject_id) AS cnt
FROM Teacher
GROUP BY teacher_id;
notes: COUNT(DISTINCT subject_id) grouped by teacher_id.

title: User Activity for the Past 30 Days I
solution:
-- 1141. User Activity for the Past 30 Days I
SELECT 
    activity_date AS day,
    COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS active_users
FROM Activity
WHERE activity_date BETWEEN DATE_SUB('2019-07-27', INTERVAL 29 DAY) AND '2019-07-27'
GROUP BY activity_date;
notes: Ending 2019-07-27 inclusive (30-day window starts 2019-06-28).

title: Product Sales Analysis III
solution:
-- 1070. Product Sales Analysis III
SELECT product_id, year AS first_year, quantity, price
FROM Sales
WHERE (product_id, year) IN (
    SELECT product_id, MIN(year)
    FROM Sales
    GROUP BY product_id
);
notes: Subquery finds the minimum year for each product.

title: Classes More Than 5 Students
solution:
-- 596. Classes More Than 5 Students
SELECT class
FROM Courses
GROUP BY class
HAVING COUNT(student) >= 5;
notes: GROUP BY + HAVING COUNT(student) >= 5.

title: Find Followers Count
solution:
-- 1729. Find Followers Count
SELECT user_id, COUNT(follower_id) AS followers_count
FROM Followers
GROUP BY user_id
ORDER BY user_id ASC;
notes: Count followers grouped by user_id.

title: Biggest Single Number
solution:
-- 619. Biggest Single Number
SELECT MAX(num) AS num
FROM (
    SELECT num
    FROM MyNumbers
    GROUP BY num
    HAVING COUNT(num) = 1
) t;
notes: Wrapping in MAX() ensures NULL is returned if no single number exists.

title: Customers Who Bought All Products
solution:
-- 1045. Customers Who Bought All Products
SELECT customer_id
FROM Customer
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT product_key) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Product);
notes: Relational division via HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT) = Total Products.

title: The Number of Employees Which Report to Each Employee
solution:
-- 1731. The Number of Employees Which Report to Each Employee
SELECT 
    m.employee_id,
    m.name,
    COUNT(e.employee_id) AS reports_count,
    ROUND(AVG(e.age)) AS average_age
FROM Employees m
JOIN Employees e ON m.employee_id = e.reports_to
GROUP BY m.employee_id, m.name
ORDER BY m.employee_id;
notes: Self join manager to subordinate on reports_to.

title: Primary Department for Each Employee
solution:
-- 1789. Primary Department for Each Employee
SELECT employee_id, department_id
FROM Employee
WHERE primary_flag = 'Y'
UNION
SELECT employee_id, department_id
FROM Employee
GROUP BY employee_id
HAVING COUNT(department_id) = 1;
notes: UNION eliminates duplicate rows between flag='Y' and employees in exactly 1 department.

title: Triangle Judgement
solution:
-- 610. Triangle Judgement
SELECT x, y, z,
    CASE 
        WHEN x + y > z AND x + z > y AND y + z > x THEN 'Yes'
        ELSE 'No'
    END AS triangle
FROM Triangle;
notes: Triangle theorem: each pair sum must be strictly greater than third side.

title: Consecutive Numbers
solution:
-- 180. Consecutive Numbers
WITH RankedLogs AS (
    SELECT 
        num,
        LEAD(num, 1) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS next_1,
        LEAD(num, 2) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS next_2
    FROM Logs
)
SELECT DISTINCT num AS ConsecutiveNums
FROM RankedLogs
WHERE num = next_1 AND num = next_2;
notes: Use LEAD(num, 1) and LEAD(num, 2) over ORDER BY id.

title: Product Price at a Given Date
solution:
-- 1164. Product Price at a Given Date
SELECT product_id, new_price AS price
FROM Products
WHERE (product_id, change_date) IN (
    SELECT product_id, MAX(change_date)
    FROM Products
    WHERE change_date <= '2019-08-16'
    GROUP BY product_id
)
UNION
SELECT product_id, 10 AS price
FROM Products
GROUP BY product_id
HAVING MIN(change_date) > '2019-08-16';
notes: Separate into changed products <= date and untouched products with default 10.

title: Last Person to Fit in the Bus
solution:
-- 1204. Last Person to Fit in the Bus
WITH RunningWeight AS (
    SELECT 
        person_name,
        SUM(weight) OVER (ORDER BY turn) AS total_weight
    FROM Queue
)
SELECT person_name
FROM RunningWeight
WHERE total_weight <= 1000
ORDER BY total_weight DESC
LIMIT 1;
notes: SUM(weight) OVER (ORDER BY turn) calculates cumulative weight.

title: Count Salary Categories
solution:
-- 1907. Count Salary Categories
SELECT 'Low Salary' AS category, COUNT(*) AS accounts_count
FROM Accounts WHERE income < 20000
UNION
SELECT 'Average Salary' AS category, COUNT(*)
FROM Accounts WHERE income BETWEEN 20000 AND 50000
UNION
SELECT 'High Salary' AS category, COUNT(*)
FROM Accounts WHERE income > 50000;
notes: UNION preserves rows even with 0 counts.

title: Employees Whose Manager Left the Company
solution:
-- 1978. Employees Whose Manager Left the Company
SELECT employee_id
FROM Employees
WHERE salary < 30000
  AND manager_id IS NOT NULL
  AND manager_id NOT IN (SELECT employee_id FROM Employees)
ORDER BY employee_id;
notes: Remember `manager_id IS NOT NULL` before `NOT IN`.

title: Exchange Seats
solution:
-- 626. Exchange Seats
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN id % 2 = 1 AND id = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Seat) THEN id
        WHEN id % 2 = 1 THEN id + 1
        ELSE id - 1
    END AS id,
    student
FROM Seat
ORDER BY id ASC;
notes: Swap logic using CASE condition on id parity.

title: Movie Rating
solution:
-- 1341. Movie Rating
(SELECT u.name AS results
 FROM MovieRating mr
 JOIN Users u ON mr.user_id = u.user_id
 GROUP BY mr.user_id
 ORDER BY COUNT(mr.movie_id) DESC, u.name ASC
 LIMIT 1)
UNION ALL
(SELECT m.title AS results
 FROM MovieRating mr
 JOIN Movies m ON mr.movie_id = m.movie_id
 WHERE mr.created_at BETWEEN '2020-02-01' AND '2020-02-29'
 GROUP BY mr.movie_id
 ORDER BY AVG(mr.rating) DESC, m.title ASC
 LIMIT 1);
notes: UNION ALL with individual parentheses per query for LIMIT 1.

title: Restaurant Growth
solution:
-- 1321. Restaurant Growth
WITH DailySum AS (
    SELECT visited_on, SUM(amount) AS amount
    FROM Customer
    GROUP BY visited_on
)
SELECT 
    visited_on,
    SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY visited_on ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS amount,
    ROUND(AVG(amount) OVER (ORDER BY visited_on ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS average_amount
FROM DailySum
ORDER BY visited_on
OFFSET 6;
notes: Moving window over 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.

title: Friend Requests II: Who Has the Most Friends
solution:
-- 602. Friend Requests II: Who Has the Most Friends
WITH AllFriends AS (
    SELECT requester_id AS id FROM RequestAccepted
    UNION ALL
    SELECT accepter_id AS id FROM RequestAccepted
)
SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS num
FROM AllFriends
GROUP BY id
ORDER BY num DESC
LIMIT 1;
notes: Friendship is two-way: UNION ALL requester and accepter.

title: Investments in 2016
solution:
-- 585. Investments in 2016
SELECT ROUND(SUM(tiv_2016), 2) AS tiv_2016
FROM (
    SELECT 
        tiv_2016,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY tiv_2015) AS count_2015,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY lat, lon) AS count_loc
    FROM Insurance
) t
WHERE count_2015 > 1 AND count_loc = 1;
notes: COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY ...) cleanly handles multiple conditions.

title: Department Top Three Salaries
solution:
-- 185. Department Top Three Salaries
WITH RankedSalaries AS (
    SELECT 
        d.name AS Department,
        e.name AS Employee,
        e.salary AS Salary,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY e.departmentId 
            ORDER BY e.salary DESC
        ) AS rnk
    FROM Employee e
    JOIN Department d ON e.departmentId = d.id
)
SELECT Department, Employee, Salary
FROM RankedSalaries
WHERE rnk <= 3;
notes: DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY departmentId ORDER BY salary DESC) <= 3.

title: Fix Names in a Table
solution:
-- 1667. Fix Names in a Table
SELECT 
    user_id,
    CONCAT(UPPER(SUBSTRING(name, 1, 1)), LOWER(SUBSTRING(name, 2))) AS name
FROM Users
ORDER BY user_id;
notes: CONCAT first character uppercase + remainder lowercase.

title: Patients With a Condition
solution:
-- 1527. Patients With a Condition
SELECT patient_id, patient_name, conditions
FROM Patients
WHERE conditions LIKE 'DIAB1%' OR conditions LIKE '% DIAB1%';
notes: Match DIAB1 at start or preceded by space.

title: Delete Duplicate Emails
solution:
-- 196. Delete Duplicate Emails
DELETE p1
FROM Person p1
JOIN Person p2
WHERE p1.email = p2.email AND p1.id > p2.id;
notes: Self join deleting the larger id instance.

title: Second Highest Salary
solution:
-- 176. Second Highest Salary
SELECT MAX(salary) AS SecondHighestSalary
FROM Employee
WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee);
notes: MAX() returns NULL cleanly if no 2nd salary.

title: Group Sold Products By The Date
solution:
-- 1484. Group Sold Products By The Date
SELECT 
    sell_date,
    COUNT(DISTINCT product) AS num_sold,
    GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT product ORDER BY product ASC SEPARATOR ',') AS products
FROM Activities
GROUP BY sell_date
ORDER BY sell_date;
notes: GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT product ORDER BY product SEPARATOR ',').

title: List the Products Ordered in a Period
solution:
-- 1327. List the Products Ordered in a Period
SELECT p.product_name, SUM(o.unit) AS unit
FROM Products p
JOIN Orders o ON p.product_id = o.product_id
WHERE o.order_date BETWEEN '2020-02-01' AND '2020-02-29'
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name
HAVING unit >= 100;
notes: Filter Feb 2020 + HAVING sum >= 100.

title: Find Users With Valid E-Mails
solution:
-- 1517. Find Users With Valid E-Mails
SELECT user_id, name, mail
FROM Users
WHERE mail REGEXP '^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*@leetcode[.]com$';
notes: Regex: start with letter, valid body, escaped [.]com.

title: 178. Rank Scores
solution:
-- 178. Rank Scores
SELECT 
    score,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS `rank`
FROM Scores;
notes: DENSE_RANK() ensures contiguous ranks with no gaps on ties.

title: 184. Department Highest Salary
solution:
-- 184. Department Highest Salary
WITH Ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        d.name AS Department,
        e.name AS Employee,
        e.salary AS Salary,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY e.departmentId ORDER BY e.salary DESC) AS rnk
    FROM Employee e
    JOIN Department d ON e.departmentId = d.id
)
SELECT Department, Employee, Salary
FROM Ranked
WHERE rnk = 1;
notes: Partition By + Filtering Top-1 using DENSE_RANK().

title: 185. Department Top Three Salaries
solution:
-- 185. Department Top Three Salaries
WITH RankedSalaries AS (
    SELECT 
        d.name AS Department,
        e.name AS Employee,
        e.salary AS Salary,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY e.departmentId 
            ORDER BY e.salary DESC
        ) AS rnk
    FROM Employee e
    JOIN Department d ON e.departmentId = d.id
)
SELECT Department, Employee, Salary
FROM RankedSalaries
WHERE rnk <= 3;
notes: Top-N per group using DENSE_RANK() <= 3.

title: 601. Human Traffic of Stadium
solution:
-- 601. Human Traffic of Stadium
WITH Filtered AS (
    SELECT 
        id, visit_date, people,
        id - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS grp
    FROM Stadium
    WHERE people >= 100
),
GroupCounts AS (
    SELECT *, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY grp) AS cnt
    FROM Filtered
)
SELECT id, visit_date, people
FROM GroupCounts
WHERE cnt >= 3
ORDER BY visit_date;
notes: Gaps & Islands: `id - ROW_NUMBER()` produces identical group tag for consecutive rows.

title: 1709. Biggest Window Between Visits
solution:
-- 1709. Biggest Window Between Visits
WITH NextVisits AS (
    SELECT 
        user_id,
        visit_date,
        LEAD(visit_date, 1, '2021-01-01') OVER (
            PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY visit_date
        ) AS next_visit
    FROM UserVisits
)
SELECT 
    user_id,
    MAX(DATEDIFF(next_visit, visit_date)) AS biggest_window
FROM NextVisits
GROUP BY user_id
ORDER BY user_id;
notes: LEAD(visit_date, 1, '2021-01-01') provides default date for last visit.

title: 585. Investments in 2016
solution:
-- 585. Investments in 2016
SELECT ROUND(SUM(tiv_2016), 2) AS tiv_2016
FROM (
    SELECT 
        tiv_2016,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY tiv_2015) AS count_2015,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY lat, lon) AS count_loc
    FROM Insurance
) t
WHERE count_2015 > 1 AND count_loc = 1;
notes: Multi-condition window aggregations.

title: 1308. Running Total for Different Genders
solution:
-- 1308. Running Total for Different Genders
SELECT 
    gender,
    day,
    SUM(score_points) OVER (
        PARTITION BY gender 
        ORDER BY day
    ) AS total_score
FROM Scores
ORDER BY gender, day;
notes: Cumulative sum: SUM() OVER (PARTITION BY gender ORDER BY day).

title: 626. Exchange Seats
solution:
-- 626. Exchange Seats
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN id % 2 = 1 AND id = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Seat) THEN id
        WHEN id % 2 = 1 THEN id + 1
        ELSE id - 1
    END AS id,
    student
FROM Seat
ORDER BY id ASC;
notes: Conditional logic & row index permutation.

title: 1158. Market Analysis I
solution:
-- 1158. Market Analysis I
SELECT 
    u.user_id AS buyer_id,
    u.join_date,
    COUNT(o.order_id) AS orders_in_2019
FROM Users u
LEFT JOIN Orders o 
  ON u.user_id = o.buyer_id 
 AND YEAR(o.order_date) = 2019
GROUP BY u.user_id, u.join_date;
notes: Must put `YEAR(order_date)=2019` in LEFT JOIN ON clause.

title: 1907. Count Salary Categories
solution:
-- 1907. Count Salary Categories
SELECT 'Low Salary' AS category, COUNT(*) AS accounts_count
FROM Accounts WHERE income < 20000
UNION
SELECT 'Average Salary' AS category, COUNT(*)
FROM Accounts WHERE income BETWEEN 20000 AND 50000
UNION
SELECT 'High Salary' AS category, COUNT(*)
FROM Accounts WHERE income > 50000;
notes: UNION preserves rows even with zero counts.

title: DataLemur: Highest-Grossing Items
solution:
-- DataLemur: Highest-Grossing Items
WITH TotalSpend AS (
    SELECT 
        category,
        product,
        SUM(spend) AS total_spend,
        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY category 
            ORDER BY SUM(spend) DESC
        ) AS ranking
    FROM product_spend
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM transaction_date) = 2022
    GROUP BY category, product
)
SELECT category, product, total_spend
FROM TotalSpend
WHERE ranking <= 2
ORDER BY category, ranking;
notes: Multi-level grouping + RANK() partitioned by category.

title: 262. Trips and Users
solution:
-- 262. Trips and Users
SELECT 
    t.request_at AS Day,
    ROUND(
        SUM(t.status IN ('cancelled_by_driver', 'cancelled_by_client')) / COUNT(*), 
        2
    ) AS `Cancellation Rate`
FROM Trips t
JOIN Users c ON t.client_id = c.users_id AND c.banned = 'No'
JOIN Users d ON t.driver_id = d.users_id AND d.banned = 'No'
WHERE t.request_at BETWEEN '2013-10-01' AND '2013-10-03'
GROUP BY t.request_at
ORDER BY Day;
notes: Join Users twice to filter banned clients and banned drivers.
